body:
VERIFIED against the code.

`requires_reading_services_auth_and_config` (cps/readingservices.py) proxies the
request untouched in two cases:

    if not config.config_kobo_sync:            -> proxy_to_kobo_reading_services()
    ...
    if current_user.is_authenticated: ...      -> otherwise proxy

`handle_check_for_changes` is therefore never entered, so the ownership filter
that keeps an owned book out of Nickel's destructive annotations GET does not
run. Measured device behaviour: if checkforchanges names a ContentId, Nickel
GETs that book's annotations and REPLACES its entire local set with the result.

Reachable windows: the device keeps CWNG configured as its reading-services host
while its Flask session expires (upstream Kobo credentials still valid), and the
interval after an admin disables Kobo sync but before the device refreshes its
service configuration.

The containment is only as strong as the weakest way of reaching the route, and
the decorator is currently the weakest.

UNVERIFIED, same family, recorded so it is not lost: only the exact path
`/api/v3/content/checkforchanges` is intercepted. A trailing slash would fall to
the `/<path:subpath>` catch-all proxy. I reasoned this from the route table but
did NOT execute it against the real url_map, and no device has been observed
sending the slash form.
title: checkforchanges containment is bypassed when Kobo sync is off or the session is unauthenticated
